newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit ends down but profit-taking limits fall.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit ends down but profit-taking limits fall.

text.p: The ringgit extended its fall on continued dollar covering, but profit-taking limited the local currency's losses, dealers said.

They said the ringgit weakened in tandem with the downtrend of other major currencies against the dollar in overseas markets. "The fall is not unexpected as the dollar is well-bid everywhere," said a local bank dealer.

He said profit-taking was evident throughout the day after the dollar's sharp rise on Monday, but at the same time there was also sufficient offshore buying of dollar/ringgit to outweigh commercial demand for ringgit by local exporters.
At the local 1000 GMT close, the ringgit was at 2.5135/40 per dollar against 2.5104/14 on Monday.

The ringgit's sudden decline on Monday was due to comments by a Bank Negara official that the bank would consider using capital controls if short-term capital played a too dominant role in fund flows to the country.
The market turned nervous because the central bank has in the past used such controls.
Dealers said the ringgit could be heading down to 2.52 a dollar though some support resistance is expected at 2.5150.
